status: written and committed BEFORE any candidate below was scored; production's own diagnostics (the integer-stats study, research/reports/nfl_discrete_alloc.md) had already been read
question: Which, if any, replacement for the NFL week board's player distributions (nfl_dfs_sim.simulate_game, the continuous legacy model) gives better-calibrated per-player statistics?

development.data: research/data/player_weeks_2022_2025.csv.gz (2025 weeks 1-12) and research/data/player_weeks_2026.csv.gz (2026 weeks 1-5: all that table holds; weeks 6-12 were never built into it and are NOT read)
development.already_used: the same 257 games the integer-stats study read: this is development data, seen
development.fit: every fitted parameter is fitted on 2025 weeks 1-12 for the development comparison (scored out of sample on 2026 weeks 1-5), then refitted on all development games for the frozen registration
development.sealed: 2026 week 13 on is never read during development (asserted in the harness)

production.what: nfl_dfs_sim.simulate_game as it runs (with_components; DraftKings points = its pinned points array); the baseline every candidate is compared with

candidates.name: constrained simulator
candidates.what: nfl_dfs_csim.simulate_game with its committed Stage 2E parameters (research/data/csim_params.json, fitted on 2022-2024 only); counts drawn, yards rounded (np.rint); nothing refitted here

candidates.name: discrete allocation, quarterback fix
candidates.what: nfl_discrete_alloc.simulate_game(pass_latent_scale=k): event counts, conservation exact; the team passing multiplier's deviation from 1 scaled by k
fitted_here: k: the grid 0.0, 0.1, ..., 1.0; the k whose development quarterbacks' passing-yard realized-over-model variance ratio is closest to 1 (ties to the larger k)

candidates.name: production with a per-position x statistic quantile mapping
candidates.what: production's worlds, each marginal mapped through G^-1 o F: F the world's own CDF, G the development empirical CDF of production's randomized PIT for that position and statistic (knots at 0, 0.05, ..., 1; each knot (count + 20 x t) / (N + 20), linear between knots, monotone). Corrects mean bias, spread and asymmetric tails per cell without one shared factor; the joint structure (copula) of production's worlds is kept; the mapped box is no longer one consistent stat line (each marginal is mapped on its own)
fitted_here: G per position (QB, RB, WR, TE) x statistic (pass_yd, pass_td, int, rush_yd, rush_td, rec, rec_yd, rec_td, dk): 19 interior knot values a cell

scored.applies_when: the projected mean is at least: yards 5, receptions 0.5, TDs and interceptions 0.05, DraftKings points 1
scored.lines: fixed off the PROJECTION only (never a model output): yards round(m x f) + 0.5 and receptions floor(m x f) + 0.5 for f in 0.5, 0.75, 1, 1.25, 1.5 (distinct, > 0); TDs and interceptions 0.5 (passing TDs 0.5, 1.5, 2.5); DraftKings points round(m x f) + 0.25 for f in 0.5, 1, 1.5 (no tie is reachable: DK scores move in 0.04 / 0.1 steps)
scored.probability: P(X > L) = (worlds above L + 0.5) / (n + 1), the same rule for every model
scored.metrics: per position x statistic: mean bias (actual - model mean), realized-over-model variance, half-line log loss and Brier, a 10-bin calibration curve, 50/80/90% central interval coverage and the floor (under the 10th percentile) / ceiling (over the 90th) split off the randomized PIT, zero mass and TD lumpiness (P(0), P(2+)) model vs real; joint: within-world DraftKings-point correlation by pair type (QB-WR, QB-TE, QB-RB, WR-WR, WR-TE, RB-WR, QB-QB opponents) against the observed correlation of residuals
scored.workload_and_shape: descriptive, production and the real box: Sleeper's projected targets and carries against the real ones (bias, dispersion index), residual skew, zero mass, TD lumpiness
